newsitem.title: UK: Copper less bearish, but upside limited - Bloomsbury.
newsitem.headline: Copper less bearish, but upside limited - Bloomsbury.

text.p: Little further upside is in prospect for copper prices at present because China will dampen down the market with sales, although the outlook is less bearish, industry analyst Bloomsbury Minerals Economics (BME) said.
In its latest statistical review BME said that the market in its estimation still recorded a global surplus of 55,000 tonnes in 1996 and the surplus is expected to grow.
Although the Chinese are likely to add to their stockpile on price dips to $0.95/lb they are unhappy to see the market much above $1.10. Current LME copper prices are around $1.05/lb.
"Thus we do not see more than a few c/lb of upside from today's price without the Chinese at least trying to damp it down with stockpile disposals," BME analyst Peter Hollands said in the report.
BME said that, price levels permitting, China can now be expected to step up offtake from the Weest now that the Japanese April 1 GSP (Generalised System of Preferences) import deadline has passed.
China has already taken copper from a number of sources, up to around 25,000 tonnes according to some estimates.
"Moreover, further foreign exchange and credit is expected to be extended to importers soon, so additional purchases for April and May shipment are likely," it said.
BME also raised its estimate of global consumption growth to four percent a year, which equates to an extra 650,000 tonnes of offtake a year.
